questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: A sort of personal connection as I have always loved the language and the nature of Norway, and I wanted to go to a destination not too different from Denmark. However, I did not know anyone in Bergen before.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nature (outdoor, hiking, trips) and availability of mandatory courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: For any question I had the university was very good and quick to help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Just be very aware of “office hours” and closing days, ‘cause you will need signatures and stamps at some point and it is nice know the deadlines — also the ones of the host university

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Start in a reasonable amount of time before, but be aware that most people also don’t look for short-term renters half a year before. I recommend
Hybel.no

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to be close to the city center, but I think the people living at student housing opportunities (which were out of the city center) had more planned/organized social activities with other students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For me it was important to live with locals for the “authentic experience”, student housing is often/mostly international students. Public transportation has a great student discount and is very accessible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had two courses (2x15 ECTS). One course was open, the other I had to apply for (restricted), but the process was simple. I received mails with good guides and deadlines.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mails!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just ask/write the course responsible or international coordinator if you have any doubts

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Courses were first and second year psychology-courses, the level was fine

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PSYK106 - Personalpsykologi (English)
PSYK208 - Affekt og kognisjon (Norwegian)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both can be recommended, the selection of courses is not very big. Having a course taught in Norwegian was a good experience

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation was cheaper than expected (student discount). In general Bergen has a lot of student discounts (shops, museums, events etc.)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined a lot of clubs!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A lot of different sports, for all students and specifically for psychology students
Party/social committees, winter bathing, knitting, hiking, board games and more

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All above, and join as much as possible (that you are interested in). It is a great way to meet local students and other internationals!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature outside of Bergen, take longer trips, stay in a cabin in the wilderness

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you want to speak danish/“danishwegian” speak slow and exchange differing words with the Norwegian ones as you learn them. Understanding and being understood can be challenging for all parties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Making relations internationals to locals

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of being outdoors in nature!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Experience nature early (summer/early fall) and often
2. Participate in things
3. Study with others (local and international friends)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends, and having experiences together!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being in a new country by myself

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
